title: First 7 Days — Embedded Engineer On-Call Readiness Checklist
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operational-first checklist to get a newly hired embedded engineer (embedded in a product team) into safe and useful on-call participation within their first seven days. Intended for people-ops, hiring managers, and the SRE partner.

Scope / Intended audience:
- New embed engineers joining product pods who will be expected to join the team's on-call rotation early (within 30 days).
- Hiring manager + tech buddy + SRE/observability owner are responsible for sign-offs.

Notes up front (notes-to-self style):
- This is a practical checklist, not a replacement for full 90-day onboarding.
- Prioritize access + runbook familiarity over deep systems knowledge in week 1.
- Expect the first couple of on-call shifts to be shadowed or paired.

Preboarding (before Day 0) — owner: people-ops + infra:
- Offer acceptance packet includes explicit on-call expectations and a short FAQ.
- Account creation: Google workspace, corporate MFA, Okta SSO — confirm success.
- Slack channels: add to #team-<pod>, #oncall-escalations, #sre-pager-duty.
- PagerDuty (or equivalent): create user, add to staging group, test a single test page and confirm receipt.
- Access checklist sent to hiring manager: GitHub, CI/CD, cloud console read-only, monitoring dashboard read access.
- Hardware/dev VM: order laptop + power adapters; preinstalled baseline image (or access to cloud dev image).
- Send short "What to expect first week" note to the new hire: link to runbook, Buddy assignment, quick wins list.

Day 0 — admin + introductions (owner: hiring manager):
- Quick welcome call (30 min): team intro, on-call culture, escalation expectations.
- Meet your buddy (15–30 min): exchange contact info and overlap times.
- Confirm all SSO/MFA/GitHub access. If missing, create a ticket and tag infra and people-ops.
- Confirm PagerDuty test success; if not successful, triage with SRE.
- Workspace setup: Slack, email, calendar, VPN, dev environment access.
- Send link to minimal runbook reading list (see "must reads").

Must-reads (Day 0–1):
- Team on-call runbook (top-level): how to acknowledge alerts, priority levels, cheat-sheet for common mitigation commands.
- Escalation matrix: who to ping for infra, app, data incidents.
- Incident postmortem template and expectations for blameless reporting.
- Quick network / service map for the product slice they own.

Day 1 — orientation + environment (owner: buddy):
- Pair with buddy to walk through a recent incident (read-only): timeline, what was tried, outcome.
- Hands-on: access monitoring dashboards (live), set personal dashboard watchlist.
- Run through a list of 5 common pager signals and the minimal triage steps for each.
- Confirm access to service logs, traces, and CI build pages.
- Verify runbook tests: walk through one runbook play and confirm steps are reproducible in dev/staging.

Day 2–3 — guided practice (owner: buddy + SRE):
- Shadow a real on-call shift (paired) — observe the flow from alert to acknowledgment to resolution.
- Small simulation: trigger a low-priority test alert (controlled) and practice the triage steps end-to-end.
- Check access notes: S3/buckets, DB read-only, service token rotation docs — confirm you can read the items needed.
- Confirm emergency contact breakdown: SMS escalation list, escalation times, timezone considerations.

Day 4–5 — independent lightweight participation (owner: hiring manager):
- Assigned a 4–6 hour on-call window to respond to low-impact alerts with buddy on standby.
- Complete two small tickets that exercise deploy / rollback or config change in staging with rollback plan approved.
- Fill out a short incident simulation report for the two practice events — use postmortem template but mark as "simulation".

Day 6–7 — assessment & sign-off (owner: hiring manager + SRE):
- Formal checklist review: confirm training items completed and access validated.
- Manager + SRE review simulation reports and confirm readiness for limited production on-call (e.g., night/weekend shadowed shifts).
- If gaps exist, schedule focused remediation (1–3 days) before production on-call.
- Add the hire to production on-call schedule as a paired/learning participant for first 1–3 rotations.

Role-specific access matrix (quick):
- GitHub: repo read + PR comment (owner signoff required for write).
- Cloud console: read-only billing + monitoring; write access gated via access request.
- Pager system: acknowledge + add note; escalation permissions managed by SRE.
- CI/CD: view builds, trigger test deploys to staging only.
- Secrets manager: read-limited for dev/staging; production access after gating.

Runbook quick-hit (to include in team runbook page):
- On alert: ACK within 5m, add initial hypothesis AND affected customers to alert ticket.
- First 10m: check service health, recent deploys, error spikes, and traffic changes.
- If no quick fix: engage L2/SRE and open incident channel (Slack + incident doc).
- Avoid major config changes without rollback plan and a second pair.

Escalation contacts (examples) — keep this short and local to team:
- Primary SRE: Jordan Rivera (pager + slack)
- Backup SRE: Priya Nair (pager)
- Team lead: Liam O'Connor (call after 30m if unresolved)
- People-ops on-call for access issues: people-ops@redwood.ai

Success criteria (end of day 7):
- Can acknowledge and make basic triage notes on a live alert.
- Successfully completed at least one paired simulation and one independent low-impact response.
- All required accesses granted or documented with open tickets for pending items.
- Manager + SRE have signed the readiness checklist.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Missing production secrets access — Mitigation: Pairing + temporary scoped tokens for first rotations.
- Risk: Overloading new hire with critical shifts too early — Mitigation: only low-impact windows and buddy pairing for first month.

Template: Manager sign-off (copy to personnel file):
- Date: _______
- Manager name: _______
- SRE reviewer: _______
- Checklist status: [ ] cleared for paired on-call; [ ] needs remediation (notes)

Open questions / TODOs (notes to hiring manager):
- Should we require a 1:1 practice incident in staging before Day 4? pros/cons.
- Confirm cross-team escalation window for APAC overlap.
- Add a short video walkthrough to runbook showing how to read a trace in our APM product.

References / quick links:
- Team runbook (confluence): confluence:ENG_ONCALL_RUNBOOK_1234
- Incident template: confluence:INCIDENT_TEMPLATE_5678
- Pager rota: confluence:PAGERDUTY_ROTATION_9012

Endnotes: This doc is intentionally minimal and tactical — copy into team runbooks and adapt. Keep it lightweight so hiring managers actually use it in the offer -> first-week flow.

Revision history:

- 2025-11-10: edits for APAC overlap and added simulation sign-off (Jordan Rivera)
